headline: Ring unveils first smart lock with hand-crank backup power
summary: Ring is entering the smart lock market with a device built to prevent being locked out when its battery dies. The lock includes a built-in hand crank, described by one outlet as a manual power dial, letting users generate power to open the door even after the battery is dead.

claims.statement: Ring is launching its first smart lock, with a built-in hand crank (called a manual 'power dial' by one outlet) to generate power and prevent lockouts when the battery dies.

sources.quote: Ring’s first smart lock can be hand-cranked when its battery dies
Ring's smart lock has a built-in hand crank to generate power when the batteries are dead.
The brand just announced a smart lock with a manual ‘power dial’ that charges the device in case it dies.
